summary.text: The whale shark is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known living fish, with an 18.8 m individual the largest reliably recorded.
It strains plankton, krill, fish eggs and small schooling fish from the sea, passing over 6,000 liters of water an hour through sieve-like gill pads.
It is listed as Endangered after its population fell by more than half over 75 years, mainly from targeted fishing, bycatch and ship strikes.

items.prompt: Despite its name, what kind of animal is the whale shark?

options.label: A fish, not close kin to whales
A small kind of baleen whale
A hybrid of whale and shark

items.explain: The name comes from its look and size; it is a fish, and like all sharks it is not closely related to whales.

items.prompt: Researchers want to recognise the same whale shark in photos taken years apart. Which feature works best?
items.explain: Its pale spots and stripes form an arrangement unique to each individual.

items.prompt: A snorkeler finds herself swimming beside a huge whale shark. How much danger is she in from the shark?

options.label: Little: it poses no significant threat
High: it bites when it feels crowded
High: it rams intruders to drive them off

items.explain: Despite its immense size, the whale shark is docile and poses no significant threat to humans.

items.prompt: How does a whale shark protect its eyes from damage?

options.label: A clear bony shield covers each eye
It keeps its eyes shut while feeding
A thick layer of mucus coats them

items.explain: Dermal denticles on the eyeball surface, plus the ability to pull the eyes deep into their sockets, protect them.

items.prompt: Whale shark numbers have fallen by more than half. What is mainly behind this?

options.label: Attacks by orcas and other sharks

items.explain: The decline is primarily the result of targeted fishing, bycatch in other fisheries and collisions with large ships.

items.prompt: Many sharks have their mouth on the underside of the head. Where is a whale shark's?

options.label: At the front of the head

items.explain: Unlike many other sharks, whale sharks have their mouths at the front of the head.
